patients.summary: Healthy undergraduate who joined the practice at 18. Three heterophile-positive mononucleosis illnesses in 2025-2026, the last complicated by mild Coombs-positive hemolytic anemia and thrombocytopenia that hematology observed and that resolved by April 2026.

documents.title: New Patient Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
New patient, 18, high school senior, coming over from his pediatric office. Starts college in the fall and expects to live on campus. Feels well. No chronic problems, no hospitalizations, no surgeries. Takes nothing regularly, no supplements.

Allergies: none to medications.

Family: maternal uncle had nasopharyngeal cancer, diagnosed at 42. Paternal grandfather had stomach cancer. Parents healthy as far as he knows.

Social: senior in high school, lives with his parents. Never smoked, no vaping. Drinks rarely, a drink or two a month at most. No drug use. Sleep is irregular around exams. Exercises, plays pickup basketball.

ROS: negative in full.

Exam: Well-appearing young man. Vitals as recorded. HEENT normal, oropharynx clear. Neck supple, no lymphadenopathy, thyroid not enlarged. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no organomegaly. Skin clear. Neuro grossly normal. Mood bright.

Screens: PHQ-2 0. AUDIT-C 1.

Assessment/plan:
1. Adult preventive care. One-time lipid check, HIV and hepatitis C screening today.
2. Vaccines: pediatric records requested; per his recollection he finished the usual teen shots. Discussed meningococcal B ahead of dorm living, he wants it, first dose given today, second in about a month.
3. Counseled on sun protection, alcohol, sleep, helmet use on his bike.
Yearly physical. Call or message with anything.

documents.title: Your Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Min-jun, cholesterol panel looks great, and the HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Nothing to repeat for years. Nurse will reach out about the second meningococcal B shot.

documents.title: RE: Your Lab Results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thanks! Does the second one have to be a full month later? I have exams the first week of February.

documents.title: RE: Your Lab Results
documents.author: RN
documents.body: At least a month after the first dose, so any time from Feb 3 on. We have late-afternoon nurse slots, so it won't cut into school.

documents.title: Records From Pediatric Practice
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Received by fax from patient's pediatric practice, 14 pages. Includes well-child visits through age 17, growth charts and immunization record.

Summary from the pediatric problem list: no active problems. No surgeries. No medications. NKDA.

Immunizations on file: infant and childhood series complete including MMR x2, varicella x2, hepatitis B x3, hepatitis A x2, polio. Tdap, MenACWY and HPV 9-valent dose 1 at the 11-year visit (Jan 2017), HPV dose 2 Aug 2017, COVID primary series June 2021, MenACWY booster Jan 2022.

Last well visit Feb 2023: normal exam, vision and hearing screens normal, adolescent depression screen negative.

Filed to chart; immunization history entered. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunization
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here after school for second MenB dose, 5 weeks after the first. Afebrile, no reaction to dose 1 other than a sore arm overnight. Given IM left deltoid, lot and expiration recorded. Observed 15 minutes, tolerated well. Series complete.

documents.title: RE: School Health Form

documents.body: Done. Filled in your vaccine dates from the pediatric record plus the MenB series from this winter, signed, and attached it back here. Have a good semester. Flu and COVID shots are available here starting late September if you're around.

documents.title: Acute Visit - Sore Throat and Fatigue
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
19 y/o, first year of college, home for winter break. About a week of feeling wiped out, low fevers off and on, and a sore throat. Also a mild ache in the upper belly and not much appetite. No cough, no rash. No sick contacts he can name. Has not taken anything for it.

Meds: none. NKDA.

Exam: Tired-looking but comfortable. Low-grade temp, vitals otherwise as charted. Tonsils with white exudate both sides. Enlarged anterior and posterior cervical nodes, mildly tender. Lungs clear, heart regular. Abdomen soft, no focal tenderness despite the upper abdominal ache he describes, spleen tip felt on deep inspiration, liver edge not palpable. No rash.

Labs today: monospot (heterophile) positive. CBC with smear: atypical lymphocytes seen.

A/P: Infectious mononucleosis.
- Supportive: rest, fluids, salt-water gargles, soft foods while swallowing hurts.
- Spleen is enlarged, so no basketball, lifting or contact of any kind until rechecked. Will see him back in about a month before he resumes.
- Avoid alcohol for now.
- Return or message for trouble swallowing liquids, drooling, breathing difficulty, left upper abdominal pain or feeling faint.
Can go back to classes when energy allows; the semester starts the 21st.

documents.title: Gym question
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Is it ok to go to the gym if I just do the bike and no weights? Also can my roommate catch it? We share a lot of stuff.

documents.title: RE: Gym question
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Checked with the doctor. Please hold off on the gym entirely until your recheck, the spleen is the concern and even moderate effort or a fall can be risky. Light walking is fine. Mono spreads through saliva, so no sharing cups, utensils or vapes and wash hands often while you're sick. Many people have already had the virus by your age, but your roommate should get checked if symptoms start.

documents.title: Update
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Just wanted to say I'm a lot better. Throat is fine, no more fevers since last week, still get tired in the afternoon but way better. Started classes today. Didn't need to take anything.

documents.title: RE: Update
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Great to hear. Keep the no-sports rule until we check your spleen. The front desk will set you up for early February, a weekend trip home or a late-day slot works.

documents.title: Follow-up - Mononucleosis
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Back about 5 weeks after the mono diagnosis. Energy essentially normal now, keeping up with classes. No fever, throat fine, eating normally. No abdominal pain.

Exam: Afebrile. Oropharynx clear, tonsils normal size without exudate. No cervical adenopathy. Abdomen soft, nontender, spleen not palpable even with deep inspiration.

A/P: Mono resolved. Cleared to ease back into the gym this week and basketball next week. Off the active list.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Outside emergency department record, received by fax 07/08/2025. Visit 07/05/2025.

CC: fever, sore throat, fatigue for 10 days.

HPI: 19M college student taking summer classes, living in campus housing. Had mono in January per his report and says this feels the same. Fevers mostly late in the day, not breaking with OTC acetaminophen. Throat so painful he has been taking only liquids the last few days. Feels run-down, has missed several days of class. Several friends in his dorm have been sick with something similar.

PMH: infectious mononucleosis Jan 2025. Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA. FHx: maternal uncle nasopharyngeal carcinoma at 42, paternal grandfather gastric cancer. SHx: never smoker, rare alcohol.

Triage vitals: T 38.5 C (101.3 F), BP 120/75, HR 88.

Exam: Fatigued, not toxic, no distress. Both tonsils enlarged with exudate, uvula midline, no trismus, handling secretions. Tender cervical lymph nodes. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Abdomen soft, spleen palpable 2 cm below the left costal margin, nontender. Otherwise unremarkable.

Labs: WBC 12.0, atypical lymphocytes 15%. Heterophile antibody positive.

ED course: oral fluids tolerated in the department.

Impression: infectious mononucleosis.

Disposition: discharged home. Rest, push fluids, no contact sports or heavy lifting until cleared by his primary care doctor. Return for inability to swallow fluids, breathing trouble or abdominal pain. Follow up with PCP this week.

documents.title: Post-ED Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: ED record from 7/5 came in this morning, called pt. Says he is drinking fine now and started soft food yesterday. Still tired, fever lower. Back at his dorm, an hour away, so set up a video visit with the PCP for tomorrow afternoon. Reinforced no sports.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Follow-up After ED Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, he is in his dorm room, consents to telehealth.

Seen in the ED 7/5 with 10 days of fever, sore throat and fatigue, monospot positive again, WBC 12.0 with 15% atypicals, spleen 2 cm below the costal margin per their exam. Since then: swallowing much better, eating soft foods, last fever two days ago. Still sleeping a lot. No abdominal pain.

We talked about this being the same picture as January. The heterophile test can stay positive for months after mono, and some people have a drawn-out or relapsing course. Treat it the same way.

Observed: alert, voice normal, breathing comfortably on camera.

Plan: supportive care. No sports, lifting or roughhousing until his spleen is checked in person; he will come for his physical in August before the fall semester and we will examine him then. Message if fevers return or he can't keep fluids down.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly physical, 19, going into his second year of college. Two bouts of mono this year, January (here) and July (ED, monospot again positive, spleen enlarged on their exam). Recovered fully from the July episode by the end of the month, back to normal energy, no fevers since. Has not done any sports since July, waiting to be cleared.

Meds: none. NKDA.
Family history unchanged: maternal uncle with nasopharyngeal cancer at 42, paternal grandfather with stomach cancer.
Social: never smoker, a drink or two a month. Will be in a dorm again.

ROS negative.

Exam: Well. Vitals as charted. Oropharynx clear, tonsils not enlarged. No cervical, axillary or supraclavicular nodes. Thyroid normal. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, no hepatosplenomegaly with careful palpation. Skin clear. Neuro intact.

PHQ-2 0, AUDIT-C 1.

A/P:
1. Mono, recovered. Spleen normal on exam today, cleared for all activity including basketball. CBC and CMP today after the two illnesses.
2. Preventive: lipids and HIV/HCV done last year, no need to repeat. Vaccines current; flu and COVID when available this fall.
Next physical in a year.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Blood counts and chemistry panel all normal, including the liver tests. You're good to go for the semester.

documents.title: Acute Visit - Fever and Sore Throat
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
20 y/o home from college for winter break. Two weeks of fevers, sore throat and exhaustion, same feel as his illnesses last January and July. OTC pain relievers and lozenges haven't touched it. Says his upper abdomen feels "puffy." No bleeding, bruising, dark urine or yellow eyes that he has noticed. Not taking any medications.

NKDA.

Exam: Febrile at 38.5, other vitals as charted. Pharynx red with exudate. Tender cervical nodes. Abdomen soft, spleen tip palpable, mildly enlarged, nontender. No jaundice. No petechiae or bruising on skin survey.

CBC this morning: Hgb 10.2, WBC 15.0, platelets 90K, 20% atypical lymphocytes. His August counts were normal.

A/P:
1. Third mononucleosis-like illness in a year, heterophile positive at the first two. Treating as a relapsing course of the same illness.
2. New anemia and thrombocytopenia. With mono the worry is immune destruction. Sent a smear for pathologist review, direct antiglobulin test, retic count, LDH, haptoglobin and bilirubin from this morning's draw; will call him with results this afternoon. Low threshold for same-day hematology input.
3. Spleen: no sports or lifting. Rest and fluids. Avoid ibuprofen and aspirin while platelets are low.
4. ED for bleeding, black stools, sudden left-sided belly pain, lightheadedness or shortness of breath.

orders.reason: Coombs-positive hemolytic anemia and thrombocytopenia with mononucleosis

documents.title: Results Call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Afternoon labs back. Smear reviewed by pathology, atypical lymphocytes confirmed. DAT positive. Retic 4.6%, LDH 388, haptoglobin <10, total bilirubin 1.9 with direct 0.3. Picture fits autoimmune hemolysis, along with the low platelets, in the setting of his mono.

Called patient. He feels the same as this morning, no bleeding, no dark urine, no chest pain or breathlessness. Explained the findings. Spoke with on-call hematology at the regional hospital: Hgb 10.2 and stable symptoms do not need admission or steroids tonight; they will see him early next week. Urgent referral placed.

Same precautions as this morning. ED for any bleeding, yellowing, cola-colored urine, faintness or worsening breathlessness. He verbalized understanding.

documents.title: Referral to Hematology
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Re: Min-jun Tanaka, DOB 12/12/2005

Thank you for seeing this 20-year-old college student, otherwise healthy, on no medications, NKDA. Heterophile-positive mononucleosis in January 2025 and again at an ED visit in July 2025, both resolving with supportive care. Normal CBC August 2025.

Seen today with 2 weeks of fever, sore throat and fatigue. T 38.5, exudative pharyngitis, tender cervical nodes, mild splenomegaly. Hgb 10.2, WBC 15.0, platelets 90K, atypical lymphocytes 20%, confirmed on smear. DAT positive. Retic 4.6%, LDH 388, haptoglobin <10, total bilirubin 1.9 (direct 0.3).

Discussed with your on-call physician today. Requesting evaluation of Coombs-positive hemolytic anemia and thrombocytopenia during a mononucleosis illness. Family history: maternal uncle with nasopharyngeal carcinoma, paternal grandfather with gastric cancer.

Copies of today's labs attached.

documents.title: Referral Scheduled
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hematology office called, referral received, pt scheduled Thursday 1/8 at 1:15. Called pt to confirm, he has it. Reminded him to bring his insurance card since it's a specialist.

documents.title: Hematology Consultation
documents.author: hematology
documents.body:
Outside hematology group. Date of consultation 01/08/2026. Received 01/09/2026.

Reason for referral: positive DAT with anemia and low platelets during infectious mononucleosis.

History: 20M, previously healthy, presented to his PCP 1/2 with two weeks of fever, pharyngitis and fatigue, his third such illness in a year. Hgb 10.2, plt 90K, 20% atypical lymphocytes, DAT positive, retic 4.6%, LDH 388, haptoglobin <10, total bilirubin 1.9. Since then the sore throat is easing and fevers are less frequent; still tired. No bleeding, no dark urine. No medications. NKDA. Family history of nasopharyngeal carcinoma in a maternal uncle and gastric cancer in a paternal grandfather.

Exam: Tired but well-appearing. Vitals as recorded. No scleral icterus. Cervical nodes still tender. Spleen palpable, mildly enlarged. No petechiae, purpura or mucosal bleeding. Heart and lungs normal.

Labs today: Hgb 10.6, plt 104K, retic 4.1%.

Impression: Mild autoimmune hemolytic anemia and thrombocytopenia accompanying infectious mononucleosis. Counts already turning upward. Positive heterophile results can persist for months, which may explain the repeated positives this year. Expect both to settle as the infection does.

Recommendations:
1. Observation. No corticosteroid at this hemoglobin with counts improving.
2. CBC weekly for now; first one next week, can be drawn at his PCP's office.
3. No contact sports or heavy exertion while the spleen is enlarged.
4. Seek care for jaundice, dark urine, bleeding or rapidly worsening fatigue.
5. Return visit in about 4 weeks.

Thank you for this referral.

documents.title: Blood Count Today
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hemoglobin up to 11.5 and platelets 131, both moving the right way since last week. Copy sent to hematology. Keep the activity restrictions for now.

documents.title: RE: Blood Count Today

documents.title: RE: Blood Count Today

documents.body: Yes. Ask campus health to draw a CBC and fax the result to us and to hematology. Fax numbers are on your after-visit summary.

To whom it may concern,

Min-jun Tanaka is under my care for a recent medical illness. His recovery is expected to take several more weeks, during which he may have reduced stamina. I support a reduced course load and flexibility with attendance through the end of February 2026. Please contact my office with any questions.

Sincerely,
Primary care physician

documents.title: Hematology Follow-up
documents.author: hematology
documents.body:
Outside hematology group. Follow-up visit 02/06/2026. Received 02/10/2026.

Interval: energy steadily better, attending classes on a reduced load, no fevers for about three weeks. No bleeding or dark urine. Weekly counts trending up.

Exam: Well. No icterus. No cervical adenopathy of note. Spleen not palpable. No petechiae.

Labs today: Hgb 12.6, plt 178K, retic 2.2%.

Impression: Autoimmune hemolysis and thrombocytopenia with mononucleosis, resolving without treatment.

Plan: Stop weekly CBCs. Repeat CBC in about 2 months through his PCP; if normal, he can be discharged from our clinic and we will send a closing letter. Spleen no longer enlarged on exam; return to sports can be decided with his PCP.

documents.title: Follow-up - Hemolysis and Thrombocytopenia
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Recheck, about 3.5 months after the January illness with Coombs-positive hemolysis and low platelets. Hematology observed without treatment; Feb counts Hgb 12.6, plt 178K. Feels completely back to normal, full course load again since March. No fevers, sore throats, bruising, bleeding or dark urine. Wants to play intramural basketball this spring.

No medications. NKDA.

Exam: Well. Vitals as charted. Sclerae anicteric. Oropharynx clear. No cervical or supraclavicular nodes. Abdomen soft, spleen not palpable. Skin without petechiae or bruising.

CBC in office: Hgb 14.1, plt 228K, WBC normal.

A/P:
1. Mononucleosis with autoimmune hemolysis and thrombocytopenia, resolved. Counts normal. Removed from active problem list. Will forward today's CBC to hematology for their closing letter.
2. Cleared for all sports.
3. Physical due in the summer; flu and COVID in the fall.

Outside hematology group, letter dated 04/20/2026, received 04/22/2026.

We reviewed the CBC from 04/15/2026 (Hgb 14.1, plt 228K). His autoimmune hemolysis and thrombocytopenia associated with infectious mononucleosis have resolved without treatment. He is discharged from hematology follow-up. Should anemia, jaundice or low platelets recur, we would be glad to see him again.

Scanned and filed.
